analysis.title: Dissecting the post-midterm technical damage
key_insights: After the US midterms produced a Democratic blue sweep, US equities fell on Thursday in a USD2.5 trillion rout on concerns that a Democratic-led Congress could tighten regulation and slow the domestic AI data-centre buildout. The Nasdaq 100 fell about 6.4%, its weakest session since Liberation Day in 2025, into correction territory and below its 200-day moving average.

The VIX rose toward 30, its highest since the onset of the US-Iran conflict, and the VXN moved above 38. Friday's payrolls came in at +165k vs +65k expected, adding to rate uncertainty and leaving any early-week stabilisation on a fragile footing.

The sell-off came in two steps. Early weakness was concentrated in the Mag-7 and Semis. Last week the Mag-7 lost about USD0.1tn while the S&P 492 lost almost USD1.3tn, versus USD0.2tn over all of October.

The Bloomberg Magnificent Seven Index reached its head-and-shoulders target near 33,000 and briefly breached it. That area matches previous resistance, the 32,600 Fibonacci retracement, the 200-day SMA and rising support from Liberation Day. Holding above it could support stabilisation, a break above 33,550 opens 34,700, and a break below 32,600 brings 29,950 into focus. RSI may be showing bullish divergence.

The SOX semiconductor index broke below its 200-day SMA for the first time since March 2025. 10,600 is the level to reclaim, and failure leaves the index vulnerable to 8,400-8,500. RSI has broken below rising support.

Nvidia may have hit a standard wave-5 target at 243, then broke rising support from the Liberation Day low. Weekend headlines about CEO Jensen Huang erased Friday's post-election technical rebound, and the stock fell below 184. Long-term support near 150 aligns with the 2025 all-time high, the 200-week SMA and the 61.8% Fibonacci retracement. 190-200 is key resistance, and 150-146 is the next support.

Software may be showing early tactical stabilisation versus semis. The software/semis ratio broke above falling resistance in place since 2025 and its 200-day SMA. A sustained move above 0.61-0.62 would support a cup-and-handle read, with potential levels at 0.85 and 0.99.

The S&P 500 is back in its previous 7,260-7,620 range after breaking below 7,484-7,507. The rising 200-day SMA is near 7,325 and range support is at 7,261. RSI near 35 is approaching oversold. A recovery above 7,484-7,507 improves the rebound case, and a break below 7,261 points to a deeper correction.

The Nasdaq 100 broke below its rising 200-day SMA near 27,984, with RSI oversold. Resistance is 27,176-27,984 then 28,750, and support is 26,182 and the lower channel boundary. Until it reclaims the 200-day, rebounds are oversold bounces, not a confirmed bottom.

The Nasdaq 100/S&P 500 ratio is testing a key support zone. A rebound would mean renewed relative strength for the Nasdaq 100 and Mag-7, while a sustained break would fit a durable rotation to broader market participation. Neither scenario is confirmed.

The Mag-7 is stabilising at structural support while semis show clear trend damage and the Nasdaq 100 stays on the defensive.
